purpose: Consistency check of the MODIS NDVI peak month against the CDL crop label (satellite command).
sources: Wardlow, B.D., Egbert, S.L., Kastens, J.H. (2007). Analysis of time-series MODIS 250 m vegetation index data for crop classification in the U.S. Central Great Plains. Remote Sensing of Environment 108(3):290–310 — in Kansas the winter-wheat NDVI peak is in late spring (April–May); corn/soybean/sorghum peaks are mid to late summer (July–August).
USDA NASS (2010). Field Crops: Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates. Agricultural Handbook 628 — planting/harvest ranges; the peak month falls between the end of planting and the start of harvest.
notes: Ranges were widened by ±1 month for the Great Plains (assumption). The peak-NDVI upper limit of 0.45 for fallow is an assumption (weed growth can raise NDVI).
